scene: SKIP: spreading news or a rumour is abstract, and spreading butter or seed would read as smeren or strooien instead.
SKIP: succeeding is a result with no action of its own; a trophy or raised arms would read as winnen.
SKIP: limiting is abstract; a fence or a cut-off line would read as afsluiten or a rule rather than the verb.
SKIP: the only picture is a coin dropped into a piggy bank, which is sparen, and the sense of sparing someone a trouble cannot be drawn.
SKIP: communicating is two people with a bar each above the head, which is praten on the A1 page.

one adult stands in a plain room holding a wooden chair off the floor with both hands, carrying it from the left side towards a pale square marked on the floor at the right, one step taken. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a chair lifted off the floor and carried from one spot to another.
avoid: a person dragging a chair along the floor (slepen); a person sitting down on the chair (zitten); a box carried to a doorway (dragen); a trolley pushed along (duwen); arrows or dotted paths.
alt: Iemand draagt een stoel met twee handen van de ene plek in de kamer naar een andere plek.

scene: two adults stand facing each other an arm's length apart. The one on the left holds out a plate with a slice of cake; the one on the right holds one flat open palm up and forward to keep it away, chin turned slightly aside, eyes on the plate. Above the head of the person refusing (palm up) floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a flat palm held up against an offered plate while the head turns away.
avoid: a plate handed over and taken in both hands (geven); a person eating the cake (eten); a hand raised in a wave (zwaaien); only a head shaking with no plate (nee zeggen); a crossed-out symbol.
alt: Twee mensen staan tegenover elkaar; de een biedt een bord met taart aan, de ander houdt een open hand ervoor.

scene: SKIP: thanking is a spoken act with two senses (thanks and owing); a nod or bow would read as groeten or buigen, and a handed-over box would read as geven.
SKIP: committing a crime or an act is abstract, and any picture would be the crime itself, such as stelen, rather than plegen.

two adults stand facing each other an arm's length apart, each holding out one object to the other: the left person an apple, the right person a loaf of bread. Both objects are caught halfway, side by side between the two pairs of hands. Both look at what they are about to receive.
must: two different objects passing in opposite directions between two people.
avoid: one box passing one way only (geven); coins and notes on a counter (betalen); two people shaking hands (groeten); a shop shelf with a price (kopen); a ring of arrows.
alt: Twee mensen staan tegenover elkaar en houden elk een ander voorwerp naar de ander uit; de voorwerpen kruisen elkaar.

scene: SKIP: a decision has no single picturable action, the same as besluiten; a fork in the road would read as kiezen and a gavel as rechtspreken.

one adult sits leaning back on a plain park bench, arms spread along the backrest and legs stretched out and crossed at the ankle, eyes open and looking at the sky, shoulders loose. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a person leaning fully back on a bench with loose shoulders and stretched legs.
avoid: a person lying in bed with closed eyes (slapen); a person sitting upright at a table (zitten); a person on a cushion with a book (lezen); a cup or a phone in the hand; zzz marks.
alt: Iemand zit achterover op een bankje met de armen langs de rugleuning en de benen uitgestrekt.

scene: SKIP: striving is an inner aim with no single action; an arrow at a target or a climber would read as richten or klimmen.

one adult stands on the left leg in an empty yard, the right leg swung forward at the moment of impact, the foot just meeting a tin can that is lifting off the ground at the right. The adult looks at the can. No goal and no ball.
must: a swung foot meeting a can that is leaving the ground.
avoid: a ball shot into a goal (scoren); a leg lifted for a step, with the can untouched (lopen); a foot on a bicycle pedal (fietsen); a fist striking the can (slaan); speed lines or dust puffs.
alt: Iemand staat op een been en schopt met de andere voet tegen een blikje dat van de grond komt.

scene: SKIP: reducing is a quantity going down; a shrinking pile or a falling arrow would need extra symbols and has no action of its own.

one adult follows through after a shot on a small grass pitch, standing on the left leg with the right leg still swinging up; a football sits in the back of a goal net at the right, the net bulging behind it, and the goalkeeper is not drawn.
must: a football lying in the net of a goal, with the kicker still in follow-through.
avoid: a foot hitting a tin can in a yard (trappen); a person dribbling a ball down the pitch (voetballen); a player with raised arms and a trophy (winnen); a ball flying wide of the goal; a scoreboard.
alt: Iemand zwaait na een schot het been door; de bal ligt achter in het net van een doel.

scene: SKIP: processing has no single action: it means working material, digesting news or coping, and each picture would read as a different verb.
SKIP: getting used to something is a gradual inner change with no single moment to draw.
SKIP: promoting is abstract; a person lifted a step up a ladder would read as klimmen or a job promotion rather than the verb.

one adult stands in an empty street holding a video camera on one shoulder, one eye at the viewfinder, the lens pointing right at a small ball rolling along the ground. The camera is a boxy shoulder model with a wide lens hood and a side screen. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a video camera on a shoulder, aimed at a moving ball.
avoid: a phone held up for a still picture (fotograferen); a person watching a television (kijken); a spotlight and a clapper board; a flash; a tripod with nobody behind it.
alt: Iemand houdt een videocamera op de schouder, een oog tegen de zoeker, en richt de lens op een rollende bal.

scene: SKIP: a greeting is a wave or a handshake, which are zwaaien and the handshake on other pages, and a nod has no single clear mark.
SKIP: hatred is an emotion with no action; a scowling face is boos and clenched fists are woede, and nothing separates it at thumbnail size.

one adult stands facing a closed plain door and knocks on it with the knuckles of a bent hand held at head height, the other arm hanging at the side; the door has a handle and no window, no sign, and no bell. Only the person and the door are in the picture.
avoid: a hand pressing a doorbell (bellen); a hand turning the handle (openen); a fist hitting a person (slaan); a mallet on a nail (hameren); sound marks.
alt: Iemand staat voor een dichte deur en tikt met de knokkels van een gebogen hand tegen het hout.
